---
title: Lay out adapter pages
description: Layout containers own the space between components, and pages respond to their own width. Follow these rules so a page works full screen and in a split workspace.
contentType: conceptual
---

Layout containers own the space between components, and pages respond to their own width. Follow these rules so a page works full screen and in a split workspace.

## Who owns spacing

Each part of a page controls one kind of space:

- **Containers**: `Stack`, `Flex`, `Grid`, and `Columns` set the gaps between their children.
- **Components**: a card or section sets its own padding.
- **Children**: a child never changes the gap that its container declares.

All containers accept the same `gap` values. `sm` is 8 px, `md` is 16 px, `lg` is 24 px, and `none` removes the gap. `md` is the default.

`PageHeader` is the one exception. It keeps a bottom margin that separates it from the page body.

## Data-binding components

`Collection` and `Resource` fetch data and repeat or fill their content. A layout container ignores their wrapper, so the items they render become direct layout items.

This grid places 1 card per database, with the grid's own gap between cards:

```ts
Grid({
  columns: 2,
  content: Collection({
    source: databaseCards(),
    content: Card({ title: { field: "name" } }),
  }),
});
```

## Responsive behavior

A page measures its own container, not the browser window. A split workspace halves the width of each page while the window stays the same size.

The built-in components adapt without any settings:

- `Grid` wraps when a column would get narrower than `minColumnWidth`.
- `Columns` stacks in containers narrower than 720 px.
- `SplitPane` stacks in containers narrower than 600 px and shows a button that opens its sidebar.

Set `minColumnWidth: "sm"` on a grid of metric tiles. The default suits panels and gives metric tiles too few columns.

## Long values

Names, paths, and error messages can be longer than their container. Built-in text wraps, badges truncate, and tables scroll inside their own box. The page itself never scrolls sideways.

## Custom components

An external adapter's browser bundle can't ship CSS, because DSUI excludes `.css` imports from the bundle. Compose built-in components, which arrive styled. If you build a [custom component](/docs/build/custom-components), use inline styles with the `--color-*` variables.
